dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Dogs are far more sensitive to alcohol than people. Beer, wine, spirits, unbaked dough and even alcohol-based hand sanitiser can cause dangerous drops in body temperature, coordination and breathing.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats are just as sensitive to alcohol as dogs, and their much smaller size means even a small spill or unattended drink is a real risk.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Alcohols in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Onions, garlic, leeks and chives — raw, cooked or powdered — damage a dog's red blood cells and can cause anaemia. Powdered forms in stock cubes, sauces or baby food are just as risky as the fresh vegetable.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats are at least as sensitive as dogs to onion and garlic, and even small, repeated amounts — such as onion powder in baby food used to tempt a sick cat to eat — can cause anaemia.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Garlic and Onion (Allium spp) Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Eating an aloe plant can cause sudden, severe diarrhoea, sometimes with vomiting, and it can lower blood sugar. Keep the plant out of reach, and call your vet if your pet shows these signs.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Eating an aloe plant can cause sudden, severe diarrhoea, sometimes with vomiting, and it can lower blood sugar. Keep the plant out of reach, and call your vet if your pet shows these signs.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Emergency — call your vet now.
dog.summary: Antifreeze tastes sweet, which is exactly why it's so dangerous — a dog will drink it readily. As little as 3–4 teaspoons can be fatal to a dog, causing kidney failure that becomes irreversible within hours if untreated.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Emergency — call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are even more sensitive than dogs — as little as 1–2 teaspoons can be fatal. A small puddle of antifreeze dripped from a car is enough to poison a cat that walks through it and grooms its paws.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Ethylene Glycol Toxicosis in Animals
Michigan State University College of Veterinary Medicine — Pets & Poison Control, Making Your Home Safer

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Dogs tolerate aspirin better than cats, but an overdose can still cause stomach ulcers, vomiting and fever. Only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed tablets.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are very sensitive to aspirin: their bodies take a very long time to clear it, so even amounts that would be fine for a dog can harm a cat. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Autumn crocus is severely poisonous. Within hours it can cause heavy vomiting and diarrhoea, stomach pain, weakness and shock, and it can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Autumn crocus is severely poisonous. Within hours it can cause heavy vomiting and diarrhoea, stomach pain, weakness and shock, and it can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)

dog.headline: Best avoided for dogs.
dog.summary: Avocado flesh contains persin, which mostly just upsets a dog's stomach rather than causing serious poisoning. The bigger risk is the pit, which can choke a dog or block its gut, and the fat content can trigger pancreatitis in a large amount.

cat.headline: Best avoided for cats.
cat.summary: Cats are less likely to eat avocado than dogs, and reported effects are similarly mild — mostly stomach upset from the persin and fat content, rather than the severe reactions seen in birds or livestock.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Avocado (Persea spp) Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Azaleas and rhododendrons can cause drooling, vomiting and diarrhoea within hours. A larger amount can also affect the heart and nervous system, causing weakness, breathing difficulty, seizures or coma, and can be fatal. A small nibble often has a good outcome with treatment, but you can't judge the amount at home, so call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Azaleas and rhododendrons can cause drooling, vomiting and diarrhoea within hours. A larger amount can also affect the heart and nervous system, causing weakness, breathing difficulty, seizures or coma, and can be fatal. A small nibble often has a good outcome with treatment, but you can't judge the amount at home, so call your vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Water with a blue-green algae bloom can poison a dog and kill it within hours, from drinking it, swimming in it or licking it off their fur. There's no antidote. Rinse your dog with clean water straight away and call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Water with a blue-green algae bloom can poison a cat and kill it within hours, including from grooming contaminated fur. There's no antidote. Rinse your cat with clean water straight away and call your vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Algal Poisoning of Animals
CDC — Preventing Pet and Livestock Illnesses Caused by Harmful Algal Blooms

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: A lick of coffee or tea is unlikely to cause a problem, but unused coffee grounds, beans, tea bags or caffeine pills are concentrated enough to seriously poison a dog.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats are at least as sensitive to caffeine as dogs, and it takes their bodies a long time to clear it, so effects can last for hours.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Chocolate Toxicosis in Animals (methylxanthines, incl. caffeine)
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Cannabis makes dogs sleepy and wobbly, and can cause vomiting, trembling and dribbling urine. Signs usually start one to two hours after eating it and can last one to three days. Deaths are extremely rare, but your dog needs to see a vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cannabis makes cats sleepy and wobbly, and can cause vomiting and trembling. Signs usually start within a few hours and can last one to three days. Deaths are extremely rare, but your cat needs to see a vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicosis in Dogs and Cats From Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: No known risk from carrot.
dog.summary: Raw or cooked carrot is a low-calorie snack many dogs enjoy. Cut it into bite-sized pieces to avoid a choking risk, especially for small dogs or puppies.

cat.headline: No known risk from carrot.
cat.summary: A small amount of cooked, plain carrot is not known to cause harm to cats, though as an obligate carnivore a cat has little use for it nutritionally.

dog.headline: Fine as an occasional small treat.
dog.summary: Most adult dogs lose some ability to digest lactose as they grow up, so cheese can cause loose stools, gas or vomiting in larger amounts. A small piece now and then is usually fine; a lot is not.

cat.headline: Best kept to a tiny amount, if any.
cat.summary: Cats lose lactase — the enzyme that digests milk sugar — as kittens grow into adults, and are, if anything, more prone to an upset stomach from dairy than dogs are.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Cutaneous Food Allergy in Animals (dairy as a common trigger)
Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine — Feeding Your Cat

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Dark chocolate is rich in theobromine, a stimulant dogs clear far more slowly than people do. Even a modest amount of dark or baking chocolate can bring on vomiting, a racing heart, tremors or seizures.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats rarely choose to eat chocolate, but if one does, the same theobromine that harms dogs harms cats too, and cats are at least as sensitive.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Chocolate Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Milk chocolate has much less theobromine than dark chocolate, so a dog usually needs to eat a lot more of it to get seriously ill — but a whole bar or more is still a real risk, especially for a small dog.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats are sensitive to the same theobromine found in milk chocolate, even though the concentration is lower than in dark chocolate.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Chocolate Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Garden mulch made from cocoa bean shells contains the same substances that make chocolate toxic, and deaths have been reported in animals that ate it. Call your vet if your dog ate some.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Garden mulch made from cocoa bean shells contains the same substances that make chocolate toxic, and deaths have been reported in animals that ate it. Call your vet if your cat ate some.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Chocolate Toxicosis in Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: No known risk from plain cooked chicken.
dog.summary: Boneless, skinless, unseasoned cooked chicken is a normal source of protein for dogs. Avoid the bones, skin, and any seasoning such as garlic, onion or heavy salt, oil or butter.

cat.headline: No known risk from plain cooked chicken.
cat.summary: Plain, boneless cooked chicken — boiled or baked with no seasoning, butter or oil — is a normal part of a cat's diet.

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: These cleaners are corrosive and can burn the mouth, throat and stomach. Burns can take up to 12 hours to show fully. Don't try to make your pet vomit, as that exposes them to the cleaner a second time. Call your vet straight away and bring the packaging.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: These cleaners are corrosive and can burn the mouth, throat and stomach. Burns can take up to 12 hours to show fully. Don't try to make your pet vomit, as that exposes them to the cleaner a second time. Call your vet straight away and bring the packaging.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Corrosive Agents in Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Daffodil bulbs are poisonous. A small nibble usually causes few or no signs, but eating more, especially a bulb, can cause vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhoea, which can lead to dehydration. Call your vet if your pet ate a bulb or shows these signs.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Daffodil bulbs are poisonous. A small nibble usually causes few or no signs, but eating more, especially a bulb, can cause vomiting, stomach pain and diarrhoea, which can lead to dehydration. Call your vet if your pet ate a bulb or shows these signs.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Dieffenbachia (dumb cane) contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Dieffenbachia (dumb cane) contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Foxglove affects the heart. It can cause stomach pain, vomiting, bloody diarrhoea, a slow or irregular heartbeat, tremors and seizures, and occasionally death. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Foxglove affects the heart. It can cause stomach pain, vomiting, bloody diarrhoea, a slow or irregular heartbeat, tremors and seizures, and occasionally death. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: The main risk from fruit pits is a blocked gut. The pits also contain cyanide, but it's only released when they're crushed or chewed, so poisoning is rare unless a pet chews up a lot of them. Call your vet if your pet swallowed a pit whole or chewed several.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: The main risk from fruit pits is a blocked gut. The pits also contain cyanide, but it's only released when they're crushed or chewed, so poisoning is rare unless a pet chews up a lot of them. Call your vet if your pet swallowed a pit whole or chewed several.

sources.label: FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet
Merck Veterinary Manual — Cyanide Poisoning in Animals

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Grapes, raisins and currants can cause sudden kidney failure in dogs. No amount is known to be reliably safe, and some dogs are affected by very small quantities while others tolerate more — there's no way to tell in advance.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats eat grapes and raisins far less often than dogs, so there's less documented experience, but the same kidney-failure risk is assumed to apply and is treated the same way.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Grape, Raisin, and Tamarind Toxicosis in Dogs
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Even a fairly small amount of ibuprofen can harm a dog, causing stomach ulcers and bleeding, and kidney damage at higher amounts. Only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed any.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are even more sensitive to ibuprofen than dogs, reacting to about half the amount. It can cause stomach bleeding and kidney damage. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Kalanchoe is one of the plants most often reported to cause serious, sometimes life-threatening, poisoning in dogs and cats. Early signs such as vomiting, drooling or tiredness don't show how serious it may become, so call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Kalanchoe is one of the plants most often reported to cause serious, sometimes life-threatening, poisoning in dogs and cats. Early signs such as vomiting, drooling or tiredness don't show how serious it may become, so call your vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Lilies cause milder stomach upset in dogs than in cats — dogs are not known to develop the severe kidney failure cats do — but it's still worth keeping these plants out of reach and calling your vet if a dog eats a large amount.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: True lilies (Lilium species) and daylilies are severely toxic to cats — even a small bite of leaf or petal, a lick of pollen, or drinking vase water can cause fatal kidney failure. This is one of the most dangerous common houseplants for cats.

sources.label: Langston, "Acute renal failure caused by lily ingestion in six cats", J Am Vet Med Assoc (2002) — PubMed
FDA — Lovely Lilies and Curious Cats: A Dangerous Combination

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Lily of the valley affects the heart and can cause a dangerously irregular heartbeat, which can be fatal. Despite its name it isn't a true lily, and it's dangerous to dogs as well as cats. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Lily of the valley affects the heart and can cause a dangerously irregular heartbeat, which can be fatal. Despite its name it isn't a true lily, and it's dangerous to dogs as well as cats. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Macadamia nuts cause a strange but usually short-lived syndrome in dogs — weakness, especially in the back legs, along with tremors and a raised temperature. The exact toxin isn't known, but the cases are well documented.

cat.headline: Not sure — no reported cases in cats, but ask your vet.
cat.summary: Macadamia toxicosis has only been documented in dogs; there isn't good evidence either way for cats, so treat any real ingestion as worth a call to your vet rather than assuming it's fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Macadamia Nut Toxicosis in Dogs
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Mothballs are toxic to all animals. They dissolve slowly, so they can keep causing harm after being eaten. Early signs are vomiting and loss of appetite; more serious poisoning can damage the blood and cause tremors or seizures. Call your vet.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats are thought to be more sensitive to mothballs than other animals. They dissolve slowly, so they can keep causing harm after being eaten, and serious poisoning can damage the blood and cause tremors or seizures. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicosis From Mothballs in Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Naproxen stays in a dog's body for a long time, so its effects last. It can cause vomiting, stomach bleeding, pale gums and weakness. Only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed any.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats may be even more sensitive to naproxen than dogs. It can cause vomiting, stomach bleeding and weakness. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Oleander is one of the most toxic common garden plants. It affects the heart, causing an abnormal heartbeat, and deaths have been reported even with treatment. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Oleander is one of the most toxic common garden plants, for cats as well as dogs. It affects the heart, causing an abnormal heartbeat, and deaths have been reported even with treatment. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Paracetamol can damage a dog's liver and blood. Dogs are less sensitive to it than cats, but only give it if your vet prescribed it, and call your vet if your dog swallowed tablets.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Paracetamol is fatal to cats: they can't break it down, and even a small amount is dangerous. Signs can appear within a few hours. Never give it to a cat, and call your vet immediately if your cat swallowed any, even if it seems fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses From Human Analgesics in Animals
FDA — Get the Facts about Pain Relievers for Pets

dog.headline: Check the label before sharing.
dog.summary: Plain peanut butter is fine in small amounts, but some "sugar-free" or "protein" peanut butters replace sugar with xylitol, which is genuinely dangerous to dogs. Always read the ingredients label — if it lists xylitol or birch sugar, treat it like the xylitol entry, not like peanut butter.

cat.headline: Not a natural food for cats.
cat.summary: Cats have little reason to eat peanut butter and it offers them no nutritional benefit, but the same xylitol-label check applies if one somehow does.

sources.label: FDA — Paws Off Xylitol; It's Dangerous for Dogs
Merck Veterinary Manual — Xylitol Toxicosis in Dogs

aliases: flea and tick treatment for dogs

dog.headline: Not sure — ask your vet.
dog.summary: Our sources describe how dangerous these products are to cats, but don't cover a dog licking or swallowing them. If that happened, call your vet and have the packaging to hand.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Many flea and tick treatments made for dogs contain permethrin or similar insecticides, which can be deadly to cats. Never use a dog product on a cat. Signs include drooling, vomiting, twitching and seizures. Call your vet immediately.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Plant-Derived Insecticide Toxicosis in Animals
Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Philodendron contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Philodendron contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

Cornell Feline Health Center — Poisons
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Best kept away from dogs.
dog.summary: Pothos contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

cat.headline: Best kept away from cats.
cat.summary: Pothos contains crystals that cause immediate, intense pain and swelling in the mouth, so most pets stop after a bite. Expect mouth pain, loss of appetite and sometimes vomiting. Serious poisoning is rare, but call your vet if your pet has trouble breathing or swallowing.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: A warm stomach is an ideal place for raw yeast dough to keep rising, stretching the stomach, and the yeast produces alcohol as it ferments — so a dog gets both a mechanical problem and alcohol poisoning from the same mouthful.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet.
cat.summary: Cats eat raw dough far less often than dogs, but the same risks — a distended stomach and alcohol produced by the fermenting yeast — apply if one does.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Bread Dough Toxicosis in Animals
Kovalkovičová et al., "Some food toxic for pets", Interdisciplinary Toxicology (2009)

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Emergency — call your vet now.
dog.summary: Rat and mouse baits use several very different active ingredients — some cause internal bleeding over several days, others attack the nervous system within hours with no antidote at all. Because you usually can't tell which type from the pellets alone, treat any ingestion as an emergency and bring the packaging.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Emergency — call your vet now.
cat.summary: Cats can be poisoned directly by eating bait, or indirectly by catching and eating a poisoned rodent. As with dogs, the active ingredient varies and the packaging is the fastest way for a vet to know what they're treating.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Anticoagulant Rodenticide Poisoning in Animals
Michigan State University College of Veterinary Medicine — Pets & Poison Control, Making Your Home Safer

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Dogs are extremely sensitive to sago palms (cycads). Eating one can cause severe vomiting and diarrhoea, followed by liver failure. The first signs often appear within a few hours and liver damage can follow over the next two to three days, so call your vet straight away, even if your dog seems fine.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Sago palm is one of the plants reported to cause life-threatening poisoning in cats as well as dogs. Early signs such as vomiting or drooling don't show how serious it is, and liver damage can appear a day or two later. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
Milewski & Khan, "An overview of potentially life-threatening poisonous plants in dogs and cats", J Vet Emerg Crit Care (2006)

entries.displayName: Play dough, salt dough and rock salt

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Homemade play dough, salt dough and rock salt contain a lot of salt, and eating them can cause salt poisoning. Vomiting usually starts within a few hours and can progress to tremors and seizures, which can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Homemade play dough, salt dough and rock salt contain a lot of salt, and eating them can cause salt poisoning, which can be fatal. Call your vet straight away.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Salt Toxicosis in Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Most slug and snail baits contain metaldehyde. It causes severe tremors, a dangerously high body temperature and seizures, starting from 30 minutes to a few hours after eating it. It can be life-threatening but responds well to prompt treatment. Call your vet immediately and bring the packaging.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Most slug and snail baits contain metaldehyde, which causes muscle spasms, wobbliness and seizures in cats. It can be life-threatening but responds well to prompt treatment. Call your vet immediately and bring the packaging.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Metaldehyde Poisoning in Animals
"Metaldehyde Poisoning of Companion Animals: A Three-year Retrospective Study" — PMC

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Vitamin D supplements can raise blood calcium to dangerous levels and cause kidney failure, which can be fatal. Vomiting, tiredness, and increased thirst and urination usually start 12 to 48 hours after eating them. Call your vet even if your pet seems fine.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Vitamin D supplements can raise blood calcium to dangerous levels and cause kidney failure, which can be fatal. Vomiting, tiredness, and increased thirst and urination usually start 12 to 48 hours after eating them. Call your vet even if your pet seems fine.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Toxicoses in Animals From Human Multivitamins and Supplements
FDA — Vitamin D Toxicity in Dogs

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet.
dog.summary: Xylitol is harmless to people but triggers a sudden, dangerous drop in blood sugar in dogs, and can also damage the liver. It's hidden in many sugar-free gums, candies and some peanut butters — always check the label.

cat.headline: Not sure — cats aren't known to be affected the same way, but ask your vet.
cat.summary: Xylitol's danger has mainly been documented in dogs. Cats rarely eat sweets, and there isn't good evidence either way for cats, so treat any ingestion as worth a call to your vet.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Xylitol Toxicosis in Dogs
FDA — Paws Off Xylitol; It's Dangerous for Dogs

dog.headline: Toxic to dogs. Call your vet now.
dog.summary: Yew is extremely poisonous. It can stop the heart, and once signs appear, treatment often can't help. If your pet has chewed any part of a yew, call your vet immediately, before any signs appear.

cat.headline: Toxic to cats. Call your vet now.
cat.summary: Yew is extremely poisonous. It can stop the heart, and once signs appear, treatment often can't help. If your pet has chewed any part of a yew, call your vet immediately, before any signs appear.

sources.label: Merck Veterinary Manual — Houseplants and Ornamentals Toxic to Animals
FDA — Potentially Dangerous Items for Your Pet
